meaning_ja: 主張と理由を一文で示す
example1: The university should pilot Option B because earlier engagement is the strongest criterion.
example2: A city should not always allocate exactly the same amount of funding to every library because local needs can differ.
caution: should not always のように always を外すと『全部だめ』と言い過ぎない。because の後ろは主張を支える基準や事実にする

pattern: I suggest that S V(原形).
meaning_ja: 提案を述べる
example1: I suggest that schools lend devices to students who cannot afford them.
example2: I suggest that policy makers improve staffing support as well as physical facilities.
caution: suggest that の後ろは動詞の原形(または should + 原形)。suggest + 人 + to V の形は使えない

meaning_ja: 条件付きで主張する
example1: Experts should recommend the policy only if the expected benefits remain strong after fairness and practical limits are considered.
caution: only if は『その場合だけ』と強く限定する。条件を満たさないときは反対と言い切ることになるので、主張の範囲に合うか確認する

meaning_ja: 起こり得る・かもしれない(断定を避ける)
example1: One country can reduce domestic emissions, but pollution may still arrive from neighboring regions.
example2: Telemedicine may lead to better access by reducing the need for long trips.
caution: can は『起こり得る・できる』、may は『かもしれない』。will・always・must にすると本文以上の強さになりやすい

pattern: A does not show / prove that B.
meaning_ja: 根拠が支える範囲を超えない
example1: A quiet period does not prove that preparedness is unnecessary.
example2: A signed form alone does not show that the person understood the study or made a voluntary choice.
caution: 強さは suggest < show < prove の順。prove は強い語なので、否定形で『言い過ぎ』を避けるのに使う

meaning_ja: 結果が示唆する(まだ断定しない)
example1: First-month results suggest that discounts can lower waste, but the effect varies by location, with Store C still leaving more food unsold.
example2: The trial suggests that students value the homework-help session before major exams, but it does not show that demand will remain high during ordinary weeks.
caution: suggest には2つの意味がある。主語がデータ・研究(results / trial)なら『示唆する』、人(I suggest that ...)なら『提案する』。提案の用法は動詞の原形を使うので、上の I suggest that の項目も参照

meaning_ja: 資料・研究がはっきり示すことを述べる
example1: Text B shows that a formal leave policy is insufficient if employees are afraid to use it.
example2: Text B shows that one visible source can produce a poor conclusion when important groups are missing from it.
caution: show は suggest より強い。主語が資料(table / text / study)のときに使い、結果が限定的なら suggest にする

meaning_ja: 結果が条件や要因に左右される
example1: Regional access depends on several factors, so increasing staff alone may not solve the whole problem.
example2: However, its benefits depend on reliable technology and patients' ability to use it.
caution: depend on の形で使う(×depend of / from)。要因が複数あるなら factors と複数形にする

pattern: what is known / what remains uncertain
meaning_ja: 分かっていることと分からないことを分ける
example1: An effective warning should communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what residents should do.
caution: uncertain は『まだ分からない点』。『間違い』『問題点』とは別の意味。分からない点は、必要な根拠まで書くと答案が閉じる

meaning_ja: 原因から結果・提案へつなぐ
example1: Regional access depends on several factors, so increasing staff alone may not solve the whole problem.
example2: It may also place more inconvenience on households with less flexibility, so efficiency and distribution should be evaluated separately.
caution: so の前が理由、後ろが結果や提案。文頭に So を置くのは避ける

meaning_ja: 前の文を理由として結論を述べる
example1: The university should therefore track both the number of new participants and the proportion who first use support before the final two weeks.
example2: The appropriate margin therefore depends on conditions such as forecast accuracy, demand variability, and backup reliability.
caution: 前の文が理由になっているときだけ使う。位置は文頭(Therefore,)か、主語の後・助動詞の後

meaning_ja: 原因から結果を示す(断定しない)
example1: Telemedicine may lead to better access by reducing the need for long trips.
example2: Investment in backup systems may lead to faster recovery when a crisis eventually occurs.
caution: lead to の後ろは結果を表す名詞。may と一緒に使うと『必ずそうなる』という言い過ぎを避けられる

pattern: A can help (to) V / allow B
meaning_ja: 役に立つ・可能にする
example1: This can help students who cannot join at a fixed time.
example2: A comparison group chosen by the same rule, or repeated measurements before treatment, can help distinguish ordinary variation from a true intervention effect.
caution: help は help + 人 または help + 動詞原形。allow は allow + 名詞(または allow + 人 + to V)

meaning_ja: 認めたうえで、本題を後ろに置く
example1: Individual effort matters, but students do not always study under the same conditions.
example2: One country can reduce domestic emissions, but pollution may still arrive from neighboring regions.
caution: 前半で認め、主張は but の後に置く。but の後ろが重くなるように書く

meaning_ja: 前の内容に対して、限界や反対を述べる
example1: However, its benefits depend on reliable technology and patients' ability to use it.
example2: However, the table covers only average delay and connection counts, not severe-event frequency or passenger volumes.
caution: 文頭に置き、後ろにカンマを付ける。前の文との関係(逆・限定)が明確なときだけ使う

meaning_ja: 譲歩しながら主張する
example1: Although Option A is expected to attract more students, the table shows that Option B produces a much higher share of early first contact.
caution: Although の節と主節の間に but は重ねない(×Although A, but B)。主節に主張を置く

pattern: Even if A, B may still ...
meaning_ja: 条件を認めても残る問題を述べる
example1: Even if a region attracts more doctors, patients may still face long travel times or limited specialist services.
caution: Even if は『仮に～だとしても』。後ろの主節に still を入れると『それでも残る』が伝わる

meaning_ja: 根拠の範囲を限定する
example1: The platform should continue the label pilot, but only as a limited intervention.
example2: However, the table covers only average delay and connection counts, not severe-event frequency or passenger volumes.
caution: limited は『範囲が狭い』。何が足りないか(何が含まれていないか)を同じ文か次の文で示す

meaning_ja: Bではなく A を選ぶ・Bではなく A である
example1: Poor digital access can contribute to continued regional gaps, so remote care should complement rather than replace face-to-face services.
example2: First, participation should be voluntary, and wearable data should be treated as a proxy rather than a direct measure of health.
caution: rather than の前後は同じ形(動詞の原形どうし、名詞どうし)にそろえる

meaning_ja: 二つを対比する
example1: The exam gives comparable evidence across students, while the assignment shows whether knowledge can be applied.
caution: while は対比の接続詞。A と B は同じ観点で比べる。文頭の While A, B の形も使える

pattern: A improves X but costs Y.
meaning_ja: 利点と代償を一文で示す
example1: It improves reliability but costs money because additional capacity may sit unused much of the time.
example2: Full anonymity in system C removes that pressure, but it also weakens accountability because careless comments are difficult to trace.
caution: 利点だけで終わらず、but の後に対応する代償を一つ具体的に書く。because で理由を足せる

meaning_ja: 両方を並べて示す
example1: Effective support therefore depends on both policy design and practical access.
example2: The university should therefore track both the number of new participants and the proportion who first use support before the final two weeks.
caution: both A and B の A と B は同じ形(名詞どうしなど)にそろえる

meaning_ja: 具体例を一つ示す
example1: For example, another leaflet will not help someone whose only available appointment is during a shift they cannot leave.
example2: For example, each week students could answer two short questions based on that week's lectures.
caution: For example の後ろには具体例を一つ。例が複数なら such as を使う

pattern: A such as B, C, and D
meaning_ja: 例を並べて示す
example1: The appropriate margin therefore depends on conditions such as forecast accuracy, demand variability, and backup reliability.
caution: such as の後ろは名詞を並べる(例示)。全部を挙げるわけではないので、並べすぎない

meaning_ja: 『かどうか』を確かめる・選ぶ
example1: Those results would show whether the system improves access without creating a new barrier.
example2: Researchers may select people who meet the study criteria, but each person must still choose whether to participate.
caution: whether は『かどうか』。目的語の位置では if と言い換えられるが、主語・前置詞の後ろでは whether を使う

meaning_ja: 条件を付けて可能性を述べる
example1: If the investment also reduces fuel risk or emissions, the long-term benefits may justify the initial expense.
example2: If everyone sees that one floor will be crowded, many students may move elsewhere and create new congestion.
caution: if 節の中は現在形にする(will を入れない)。主節は may で可能性にとどめる

pattern: In contrast, ... / On the other hand, ...
meaning_ja: 二つのものを対比する(補充)
example1: Urban residents can reach a hospital within minutes. In contrast, rural residents may need to travel for an hour.
caution: 対比の例を並べる文で使う。However(前の主張への反論)とは使い分ける

pattern: not only A but also B
meaning_ja: 複数の点を足して強調する(補充)
example1: The policy is not only expensive but also difficult to explain to residents.
caution: not only A but also B の A と B は同じ形(形容詞どうしなど)にそろえる

pattern: A unless B / as long as B
meaning_ja: 条件を述べる(補充)
example1: Remote care cannot replace visits unless patients can use the technology.
example2: A new rule is acceptable as long as exceptions are allowed.
caution: unless は if ... not の意味。unless の中に否定語を重ねない(×unless ... not)

meaning_ja: 理由や根拠を足す(補充)
example1: In addition, the program should be evaluated after one year.
caution: 原因と結果ではなく『足す』ときの接続語。Therefore / So と混同しない

meaning_ja: 前の原因による結果を述べる(補充)
example1: As a result, fewer students used the library on weekends.
caution: 前の文に明確な原因があるときに使う。証拠がまだないときは、As a result ではなく may lead to を使う
